name: Alopecia-Intellectual Disability-Hypergonadotropic Hypogonadism Syndrome
aliases: Alopecia with Intellectual Disability and Hypergonadotropic Hypogonadism

criteria.description: Presence of congenital or early-onset alopecia
Mild to moderate intellectual disability confirmed by neuropsychological assessment
Biochemical evidence of hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (elevated gonadotropins with low sex steroids)
Characteristic facial features including broad nasal bridge and micrognathia
Postnatal growth retardation or short stature

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: alopecia, intellectual disability, and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by biochemical and neurodevelopmental assessments; genetic testing may aid confirmation.

laboratory: Elevated serum luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing hypoplastic or streak gonads
Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific
genetic: No single gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance
Genetic testing may exclude other syndromes

distinguishingFeatures: Cardiac anomalies such as coarctation of the aorta
Female external genitalia with absent uterus
Normal or elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea with absent secondary sexual characteristics
Rapid progression of alopecia or scalp inflammation
references: Orphanet: Alopecia-intellectual disability-hypergonadotropic hypogonadism syndrome, ORPHA:1014
